newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - 3Com firms, Outback off.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - 3Com firms, Outback off.

text.p: 3Com Corp shares climbed 1-3/4 to 35-3/8 preceding Friday's market open on news of quarterly earning that were slightly ahead of Wall Street estimates, which were guided lower by the company last month.
After the closing bell last night, 3Com said it earned $0.47 per share in the fiscal third quarter, $0.01 per share ahead of the First Call analyst consensus forecast.
On February 10, 3Com warned earnings for the quarter would be short off the Wall Street outlook, then at $0.60 per share.
The computer networking company netted $0.42 per share one year ago.

Elsewhere, Outback Steakhouse Inc were burned after the restaurant chain warned that earnings for the quarter ending March 31 will fall short of analysts' expectations of $0.40 to $.041 per share by 10 to 12 percent.
The shares traded traded as low as 17, off 6-5/8, in active third-market trade, but edged up to 18 as the morning progressed, traders said.
The company attributed the shortfall to soft sales in February and March at its restaurants.
Kodak stock fell to 85 from 88-1/4 after the company said this morning sales in the first two months of 1997, excluding imaging revenues, have been flat versus one year ago.
IVAX Corp shares fell to 10-1/4 from 12-3/8 ahead of the market open on news the company's $1.6 billion merger with Bergen Brunswig Corp has been called off.
Bergen, which made no moves before the market open, said it intends to sue IVAX for breach of contract.

Nike Inc shares were indicated to trade up 1-1/2 to 69 after the sporting footware and apparel company reported fiscal third quarter earnings last night of $0.80 per share, $0.10 per share above the Wall Street consensus estimate compiled by Zack's Investment Research.
The company earned $0.45 per share one year ago.
Revenues for the most recent quarter rose to $2.42 billion from $1.58 billion.
